findings.reason: the fingerprint's entire purpose is to move when a plan's prose is rewritten, so a second, independent definition of what a data-reckon block is can drift from the owner's parser and silently stop catching the one edit the review exists to catch; the plan should name _plan_html.py as the owner of the authored-prose span rather than fork a parser.
findings.text: plan_fingerprint digests "the body text outside every data-reckon block" using its own _AuthoredProseParser (raw html.parser) although the module already imports the plan-document parser owner reckon/_plan_html.py (read_state) and reckon/doccheck.py::_prose_text is a second existing prose extractor

findings.reason: it is an internal refactor of plumbing already landed; the record shape, fingerprint keying and dispatch-gate decisions the plan makes are unchanged by routing the layout through a shared helper in review.py.
findings.text: plan_review_path (and _target_path at 318) re-derive the store layout — <review_store_root>/<project>/<name>.json plus a `.at-<blob8>` sibling for a second record of one key — that reckon/crew/review.py::review_path:992 already owns, differing only in the filename stem

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — reckon/crew/plan_review.py hides substantial behaviour behind a small named interface: the content fingerprint (metadata-scalar normalisation plus the derived-scalar exclusions, plan_review.py:66-101,236), the store layout and its idempotent re-store/sibling rule (store_plan_review, _target_path), the report→record grammar (parse_review_report, plan_review.py:709) and recurrence counting (declined_recurrence) sit behind store_plan_review/read_plan_review/plan_fingerprint — not many thin wrappers over one mechanism.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — plan_fingerprint's authored-prose extraction forks the plan-document parser instead of extending its owner; and the store path/sibling convention is re-derived from the code-review store's owner.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan and its design brief (c-20260925T1210, D5/D6) name the machinery they extend rather than restate it: the code-review store and reflex (reckon/crew/review.py, reckon/crew/recovery.py::dispatch_review_for_run), the promotion-boundary exempt predicate (_is_review_node), the plan-document reader (reckon/_plan_html.py::read_state) and the interface-budget counter (reckon/interface_counts.py, whose four families public_definitions/cli_options/mcp_views/refusal_families the plan §3 names as its figures), and the code reuses each.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one layer-over-existing-machinery the plan adds, §3's prior-art-and-depth review over the build skill's reuse-map rule, states in its own text why the machinery cannot simply be extended (§3: the rule is "a coordinator currently remembers to apply", and the review makes it run without being remembered); D6 likewise records that plan-review dispatch extends the review reflex in recovery.py rather than copying it.
